subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The First Electric Cars
description: A quick win: understand The First Electric Cars.

hook.text: Electric cars aren't new. In the 1890s, they were more popular than gasoline cars.

buildup.text: They were quiet, easy to start, and didn't require hand-cranking like dangerous gas engines.

discovery.text: By 1900, electric cars made up about a third of all vehicles on American roads.

twist.text: Women preferred electrics because they didn't need physical strength to start or operate.

climax.text: Thomas Edison even worked on better batteries for them, predicting electrics would dominate.

punchline.text: Edison was right—he was just a century early.

quiz.question: What share of US vehicles were electric around 1900?
